news.title: Punjab CM gives property rights to houses built in Lal Lakir
news.para: Bhagwant Mann's recent announcement marks a significant step forward for families in Punjab by initiating the distribution of property ownership certificates. This measure, part of the Mera Ghar Mere Naam scheme, aims to formally recognize home ownership, especially in Lal Lakir, while enhancing property records across approximately 4,000 villages through innovative drone surveys and advanced mapping techniques.

news.title: Chandigarh administration demolishes 80 illegal structures in Manimajra
news.para: The Chandigarh Administration launched a demolition operation at Shastri Nagar, targeting unauthorized structures on agricultural land. Early in the morning, teams dismantled around 80 illegal buildings, reclaiming approximately 6 acres of occupied farmland near the local meat market. The collaboration of various departments ensured a safe and effective demolition process, reinforcing the administration's strict stance against illegal constructions throughout the city.

news.title: Institutional investments in Indian real estate rise 39% to $5.9 billion in Jan-Sep 2026: Report
news.para: From January to September 2026, Indian real estate attracted $5.9 billion in institutional investments, primarily driven by domestic players who invested $3.5 billion. The office sector alone secured $2.2 billion exclusively from local sources. Additionally, multi-city deals surged, contributing significantly to the overall investment landscape, showcasing a vibrant and diversified asset class dominance in the market.

news.title: Chandigarh administration finally takes up long-pending issues of housing societies
news.para: The Chandigarh administration has taken decisive steps to tackle the challenges faced by cooperative group housing societies. By withdrawing the controversial 1.2 factor, the administration aims to drastically cut conversion charges, a move that comes after nearly four years of negotiations and discussions. Residents have long pushed for the Estate Office to oversee the conversion process, and the administration is also making strides towards resolving unearned increase concerns.

news.title: Goa CZMA seeks removal of Carmona land from CRZ in CZMP maps
news.para: GCZMA has written to NCSCM to request the removal of certain land from CRZ classification. This request follows the hotel's claim that the land was mistakenly classified as khazan in CZMP. A site inspection found that only part of the land qualifies as khazan due to several factors. The inspection by WRD confirmed the absence of essential features that define khazan land.

news.title: GDA plans ‘Gurukul City’ in New Gorakhpur, project launch around Diwali
news.para: The Gorakhpur Development Authority has unveiled ambitious plans for the upcoming Gurukul City, which will span over 400 acres with an initial phase encompassing 100 acres. This residential project aims to cater to Gorakhpur's increasing housing needs as the city evolves into a booming urban hub. Situated conveniently near numerous educational and security institutions, construction is anticipated to kick off by Diwali, contingent on final approvals.

news.title: Centre approves ₹65 crore for geo-spacial based survey of unauthorised colonies
news.para: The Centre has greenlit a substantial project valued at Rs 65 crore under the DRISHTI initiative, aimed at granting property ownership rights to residents in unauthorized colonies of Delhi. This endeavor will employ a geographic information system survey for precise mapping and verification of property boundaries. Furthermore, to accelerate property registrations, PM-UDAY cells will be set up in 13 districts, significantly improving legal security for families in these areas.

news.title: Haryana RERA rejects Tata Primanti buyers’ claims after conveyance deed execution in Gurugram
news.para: In a recent ruling, the Haryana Real Estate Regulatory Authority rejected a complaint against Tata Housing linked to its Sector 72 project. The buyers had executed the conveyance deed without any objections or reservations. The authority noted a lack of coercion or unfair practice in this case, highlighting that the occupation certificate was obtained before the buyers' allotment, which impacts the validity of post-deed claims.

news.title: SC seeks report on Chambal sand mining, calls impact on ecosystem ‘disastrous’
news.para: The Supreme Court has mandated the Central Empowered Committee to investigate the ramifications of riverbed sand mining, citing significant damage to river ecosystems and the risk to endangered species. States including Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh must provide affidavits confirming compliance with prior orders. This move aims to curb illegal sand mining activities and safeguard the National Chambal Gharial Sanctuary, with the next hearing scheduled for November 4.

news.title: Intensify drive against illegal sand mining in Gaya: Bihar agriculture minister
news.para: Vijay Kumar Sinha has called for heightened enforcement against illegal sand mining and transportation activities. He stressed the importance of collaboration among the district administration, police, and mining officials. Starting October 15, there will be stringent monitoring of all sand ghats to ensure compliance. Officials reported significant raids this fiscal year, leading to many vehicle seizures and arrests, with penalties collected seeing a marked increase compared to the previous year.

news.title: Pune civic body makes land acquisition department's NOC must for building permission along proposed roads
news.para: Pune Municipal Corporation has mandated no-objection certificates from the land acquisition department for construction near proposed road-widening. This directive aims to ensure the planning process is followed and uniformity is maintained across construction permissions. All new constructions and extensions will require verification of affected plot areas and road-widening status. The responsible civic officials will be held accountable for non-compliance with the new rules.

news.title: Server yet to come back to life, Kolkata civic body extends property tax rebate deadline till October 31
news.para: The Kolkata Municipal Corporation has announced an extension of the property tax rebate period to October 31 in light of persistent server issues. Taxpayers and flat buyers have been struggling with online transactions, as technical glitches hinder payment processes and certificate acquisition. Experts warn these malfunctions could stem from a possible cyber attack on the data center.

news.title: Delhi: 45 JJ clusters identified for in-situ redevelopment under master plan 2047
news.para: Delhi Development Authority has begun the process of in-situ rehabilitation of 45 JJ clusters across the city. This initiative is part of the Master Plan Delhi 2047 and aims to benefit over one lakh residents. The authority has requested proposals to appoint transaction advisers for preparing feasibility reports on these projects. The rehabilitation is intended to improve housing and civic infrastructure for existing slum residents.

news.title: Did Suraksha Group adhere to map? Uttar Pradesh government's panel to assess
news.para: The UP government has formed a five-member committee to investigate Suraksha Group's operations at Jaypee Wish Town. Recent meetings have involved homebuyer representatives discussing the status of construction and financial management. Prior assessments highlighted significant delays in building completion, with several towers unfinished. Suraksha has made some progress on halted projects and has begun offering possession to homebuyers.

news.title: Homebuyers can claim compensation for delay even after taking possession: Punjab & Haryana HC
news.para: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has reaffirmed that acquiring possession of a flat doesn't forfeit homebuyers' entitlement to seek compensation for delays. It set a reasonable timeframe for filing grievances about late possession, stemming from appeals on Emaar India's Gurgaon Greens project. Additionally, the court made it clear that developers' payments don't absolve them of statutory responsibilities, urging buyers to pursue claims even when conveyance deeds are executed.

news.title: New York's Chrysler Building finally finds a buyer
news.para: A US real estate firm announced Wednesday it is buying the Chrysler Building and will undertake a vast makeover of the Art Deco landmark that dominates New York City's skyline.  They will also pay rent to Cooper Union, a New York college that owns the land on which the Chrysler Building stands, as part of a 150-year ground lease.

news.title: After RBI policy rate hike, several banks raise lending rates
news.para: In a response to the Reserve Bank of India's recent hike in the benchmark interest rate, several leading banks have amended their lending rates accordingly. Punjab National Bank set its Repo Linked Lending Rate at 8.35 percent, effective from October 8. Indian Bank has increased its lending rate to 8.20 percent, while Bank of Baroda has set its new rate at 8.15 percent.

news.title: Brookfield to acquire 10.5 million sq ft ESR logistics portfolio; commits ₹4,300 crore
news.para: Brookfield will acquire a 100% interest in ESR India’s 10.5 million sq ft industrial and logistics portfolio across six metro clusters, marking its entry into the segment in India. The company has committed ₹4,300 crore towards the acquisition and future development of the portfolio.

news.title: Landmark Group raises ₹330 crore from SBI for  commercial project in Gurugram
news.para: Landmark Group has secured ₹330 crore in construction finance from State Bank of India for Landmark One, its upcoming commercial development on Golf Course Extension Road in Gurugram.

news.title: Bhubaneswar: Revenue loss of ₹30 crore for BMC likely this year if commercial operations in residential buildings is stopped
news.para: Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation faces a projected revenue shortfall of at least Rs 30 crore this fiscal year due to adherence to Supreme Court mandates restricting the commercial use of residential properties. In efforts to mitigate this financial setback, the civic body plans to increase tax income by assessing previously unlisted buildings.
